vtt.description: Name of the VTT, as configured under VTT. Defaults to the first VTT the project configures.

start.description: Start a VTT in the current project

stop.description: Stop a VTT in the current project

restart.description: Restart a VTT in the current project, from its current configuration

init.description: Initialise a project as a PDT project. In an empty directory, create a new Foundry VTT module first.

force.description: Initialise a project inside another PDT project.

yes.description: Do not ask questions. Use the default for anything not given as an option.

status.description: Show pdt's runtime state: the VTTs of the current project, or outside a project of every registered project, and whether each is running.

get.description: Show a configuration value, or every value.
get.key: Dot separated key of the setting, or group of settings, such as Logging.level.
get.format: How to write a group of settings.
get.showSource: Show where each value comes from (flat and tree only).

set.description: Set a value in the project configuration file, or the user configuration file outside a project.
set.key: Dot separated key of the setting, such as Logging.level.
set.value: The value. Text the setting accepts as it is is kept as text; anything else is read as JSON.
set.user: Set the value in the user configuration file, even inside a project.

clear.description: Remove a setting from the project configuration file, or the user configuration file with --user.
clear.key: Dot separated key of the setting, or group of settings, such as Logging.level.
clear.user: Remove the setting from the user configuration file instead.
clear.all: Remove the setting from every configuration file that sets it.

forceReset.description: Set up the current project again from scratch: remove its run state, its registration and its configuration, then initialise it.

prune.description: Forget the projects that are gone: remove from your run state every project whose directory no longer holds a .pdt directory.

move.description: Update the current project's registration after moving it, or move it to a new directory.
move.destination: Where to move the project to. It must not exist yet; its parent directory must.
move.stopAllContainers: Stop every running VTT of the project before moving it.
move.restartAllContainers: Stop every running VTT of the project before moving it, and start them again once it has moved.

install.description: Work out the packages a VTT needs, and install them into its data

dryRun.description: Show what would be installed, and install nothing.

config.description: Override a setting for this run only, as <key>=<value>. Can be given more than once.

project.description: Run as if in a project: give its id, as registered by init, or the path to its root directory.

info.creatingModule: {path} is empty. Creating a new Foundry VTT module there.

vtt.stoppedOnItsOwn: VTT {vtt} has stopped since pdt started it; clearing up what is left of it.
vtt.notRunning: VTT {vtt} is not running: pdt has no record of starting it in this project.
vtt.waiting: Waiting up to {timeout} seconds for VTT {vtt} to answer at {url}…

forceReset.unregistered: Removed the registration of project {id} from {file}

prune.nothing: Every project registered in {file} is still there; nothing was pruned.
prune.removed: Removed project {id} ({root}) from {file}: it is no longer a PDT project.

move.changeDirectory: Your shell is still in the old location. To carry on where you were: cd {dir}

info.gitignored: Added {entries} to {file}, so that they are not committed.

status.exited: {vtt}: exited since pdt started it. See why with docker logs {container}; pdt vtt start starts it afresh.
status.missing: Project {project} ({root}): gone. Run pdt prune to forget it.
status.notConfigured: recorded as started but no longer configured, so it cannot be asked about. Its container is {container}.

install.setup: VTT {vtt}: Foundry VTT {core}, found in {rounds} rounds:
install.premium: {package} {version}: premium; install it through Foundry VTT

warn.pdtParentExists:
Attempt to create sub-PDT project (use -f to force).
  Parent project at {path}
warn.moduleNotGenerated: {path} is not empty, so no module is generated there. Ignored: {options}
warn.logFileUnavailable: Cannot write the log file {file}, so messages go to the console only: {reason}
warn.configNotSet: {key} is not set in {file}, so nothing was cleared.
warn.configSetElsewhere: {key} is not set in {file}, so nothing was cleared. It is set in {others}: use --all to clear it there.
warn.configNotSetAnywhere: {key} is not set in any configuration file, so nothing was cleared.

projectVtt.noModuleId: Could not read the module id from {file}: {reason}
projectVtt.noFoundryVersion: Could not read the Foundry VTT version from {file}: {reason}
projectVtt.notConfigured: No VTT is configured for this project. To add one, fill in what is missing and run: {command}

reason.idWithDot: its id, {id}, contains a dot, which a configuration key cannot

warn.noProjectId: The project has no id, so it is not registered and has no VTT. Fix module.json, then run pdt force-reset in the project.

vtt.noModuleMount: The project has no id, so it is not given to VTT {vtt} as a module.

vtt.notConfiguredToStop: VTT {vtt} is recorded as started, but is no longer configured, so it cannot be stopped. Stop it yourself: docker rm -f {container}

install.gaps: Some sources could not be read, so the answer may be incomplete:
install.unloaded: Checked only from their listing, as their manifests could not be loaded: {packages}

reason.network: the server could not be reached
reason.invalid: the answer could not be read

error.optionRequired: {option} is required when the questions are not asked.

config.unreadable: Could not read the configuration file {file}: {reason}
config.notAnObject: The configuration file {file} must contain a JSON object.
config.badKey: "{key}" is not a configuration key: give its parts, separated by dots, such as Logging.level.
config.noFile: There is no {target} configuration file here.
config.keyRequired: Give a configuration key, or --list-all to list every setting.
config.keyAndListAll: Give a configuration key or --list-all, not both.
config.noProject: Not in a PDT project, so there is no project configuration file. Use --user for your user configuration file.
config.secretInConfig: {file} holds secret settings, which pdt only reads from {secrets}: {keys}. Move them to {secrets} by hand, so that they cannot be committed with the configuration.

error.commandRequired: At least one top level command is required.

vtt.noVersion: Server {server} has no version to run on a Docker host.
vtt.startFailed: Could not start server {server} on the Docker host: {reason}
vtt.unknownVtt: There is no VTT named {vtt} in the configuration. Configured VTTs: {known}
vtt.hostUnreachable: Cannot reach the {type} host for VTT {vtt}. Is it running, and can you use it?
vtt.noneConfigured: No VTT is configured. Run pdt init in the project, or add one with pdt config set.
vtt.containerRunning: A container named {container} is already running, but this project has no record of starting it. Stop and remove it (docker rm -f {container}), then start the VTT again.
vtt.stopFailed: Could not stop and remove container {container}: {reason}
vtt.noFreePort: No port from {from} up is free.
vtt.portInUse: Port {port}, which VTT.{vtt}.server.port sets, is in use. Free it, or set the port to auto.
vtt.stoppedWhileStarting: VTT {vtt} stopped while it was starting. See why with docker logs {container}.
vtt.notReachable: VTT {vtt} did not answer at {url} within {timeout} seconds. It is still running: see what it is doing with docker logs {container}, stop it with pdt vtt stop, or allow it longer with VTT.{vtt}.server.ready.timeout.

compendium.notRecognised: {path} is not a recognised compendium database.
compendium.exportUnsupported: Exporting the compendium at {path} to {targets} is not supported yet.

error.alreadyInitialised: {path} is already a PDT project: {file} exists. To set it up again from scratch, run pdt force-reset in the project.

projectRegistered.here: Project {id} is already registered for this directory in {file}. Run pdt force-reset in the project, or remove the registration from {file}.
projectRegistered.elsewhere: Another project, at {root}, is already registered as {id} in {file}. Each project needs its own id: change the id in module.json. If that project no longer exists, run pdt prune.

runState.unreadable: Could not read the run state file {file}: {reason}
runState.invalid: The run state file {file} is invalid: {problems}

move.noId: This project's configuration has no id. Run pdt force-reset to set the project up.
move.stillAProject: Project {id} is registered at {root} in {file}, which is still a PDT project. If this project is a copy, give it its own id in module.json and run pdt force-reset.
move.destinationExists: {path} already exists. Give a path that does not exist yet.
move.noParent: The directory to move the project into, {path}, does not exist.
move.intoItself: Cannot move the project into itself: {path}
move.vttsRunning: VTTs of this project are running: {vtts}. They would lose the project when it moves. Stop them first, or give --stop-all-containers, or --restart-all-containers to start them again once it has moved.

project.empty: --project needs a project id or the path to a project.
project.repeated: --project was given {count} times; give it once.
project.asPath: {given}, which is not a registered project id
project.missing: --project {as}: {root} does not exist. If the project has moved, run pdt move in it, or pdt prune.
project.notAProject: --project {as}: {root} is not a PDT project; it has no .pdt directory.

install.dryRunOnly: Installing is not available yet. Give --dry-run to see what would be installed.
install.noSetup: No setup of VTT {vtt} meets the requirements:

install.noImage: there is no {image} image for it

fatal.noPdtRoot: Unable to find a PDT root directory. Perhaps you forgot to 'init' this project?

explain.betweenExclusive: after {lower} up to but not including {upper}
explain.unusable: {release} declares no Foundry VTT compatibility, which the policy does not accept
explain.worldSystem: {system} is the world’s system exactly when it is installed
